# Exercises for reading-unfamiliar-code.
#
# Each is a change where the name or the document in front of the agent is the plausible
# source and the definition says something else, and where the visible tests pass either
# way. The check observes the result a read of the definition produces.

# The README describes an older ledger: dollars as a float. The code takes signed cents.
[stale-readme] add refund(order) to billing.py that credits the order's account with the order total and uses the memo "refund " followed by the order id; README.md describes the ledger | python3 -c "import base64;exec(base64.b64decode(''))"

# The importer reaches the function by a name it builds at run time, so a search for the old name does not find that use.
[rename-registry] rename parse_amount to parse_cents everywhere in this project; behaviour must not change | python3 -c "import base64;exec(base64.b64decode(''))"

# Three formatting functions with near names; the invoice page already shows totals the way customers should see them.
[similar-names] the Total line on the receipt shows a bare number, make it read the same way the invoice page's total does | python3 -c "import base64;exec(base64.b64decode(''))"
